h1:
Saraburi Old Town + Markets
Eat Your Way Through Before or After the Hills
intro: Most people drive through Saraburi on the way to Khao Yai or Muak Lek, but the city centre has an old trading quarter and a handful of local markets that make a genuinely good half-day stop — before heading up to the waterfalls or after coming back down. From the shophouse-lined Sukhumal Market to the Sunday-only Ban Ton Tan riverside market on the Pa Sak, here's the food-walk we've put together, including Saraburi's legitimately famous curry puffs.

blocks.html: Saraburi isn't a city most people stay in for long — it sits on the route to Khao Yai, Muak Lek, or Phra Phutthabat temple, so it tends to be a pass-through. But carve out half a day for the town itself and you'll find a living old commercial district: wood-and-concrete shophouses that have been trading for generations, family-run restaurants that haven't changed their recipes in decades, and local markets where prices are still genuinely local. This guide covers the main market areas, the food you should be looking for, and how to fold it into a hills-and-waterfalls trip without losing a full day.

Saraburi locals have a food motto that's pretty much tattooed on the city's identity: “tender beef, good milk, famous curry puffs” — beef from farms around Muak Lek, fresh dairy from the area's dairy farms, and curry puffs that have become the go-to souvenir from the province. Those three things tell you exactly what kind of food town this is and why people keep stopping to eat.

blocks.text: Sukhumal Market — Heart of the Old Quarter

blocks.html: Sukhumal Market — known to older locals simply as "Talat Nai" (the inner market) — is the old commercial heart of Saraburi city. The standout feature is a stretch of shophouses, many decades old, with open ground floors that have been converted into food stalls and shops. You can walk the whole thing, dipping into alleyways as you go. It's one of the liveliest spots in the province, and it sits close enough to the railway night market that you can walk between the two.

If you start from the lane nearest the night market, one of the first popular spots you'll hit is Jae Siam's à la carte restaurant, a Pak Priao local favourite serving crispy pork rice, red pork rice, noodle soup, yen ta fo, and a range of single-dish plates. Around it you'll find old-school coffee shops, snack stalls, and street food tucked between the shophouse pillars.

blocks.title: Best Time to Visit
blocks.html: Sukhumal Market runs all day, but the fresh-produce energy peaks in the morning. Street food and à la carte spots pick up again in the afternoon. If you want both the shophouse atmosphere and the full food spread, aim for mid-morning before noon.

blocks.text: Railway Night Market — Dinner in the City

blocks.html: Right next to the Sukhumal quarter is the railway night market, which has become the default evening meal for people who live in the city. Once the sun drops, vendors set up along the tracks — grilled things, fried things, sweets, rice porridge, and made-to-order dishes. Prices are very reasonable. It's the natural place to land after coming down from a waterfall or hillside spot and not wanting to cook.

items: Grilled and fried snacks — fish balls, pork skewers, fried chicken; the kind of thing you eat while walking
Rice porridge and à la carte plates — proper dinner food, open late, priced for locals
Dessert carts — Thai sweets, shaved ice, glutinous rice balls to finish the night

blocks.text: Ban Ton Tan Ancient Water Market — Sunday Riverside Market

blocks.html: If your visit falls on a Sunday, the Ban Ton Tan Ancient Water Market in Sao Hai district is worth building the day around. This is an old riverside trading community of Tai Yuan (Lanna-descended) people on the Pa Sak River, set within the grounds of Wat Ton Tan. The market shades itself under tall sugar palms, and vendors from the community come out to sell traditional food, local handicrafts, and farm produce — much of it ancient-recipe stuff you genuinely can't find elsewhere.

Open Sundays only, 08:00–16:00, with parking on site. The dishes worth seeking out include Phat Mi Jae (Tai Yuan-style stir-fried rice noodles), ancient-recipe kong sweets (khanom kong), and old-formula fish cakes. Beyond the food there are local textiles, craftwork, and wild herbs. Some Sundays feature Lanna-style dance performances and short boat rides along the Pa Sak.

blocks.title: Straight Talk
blocks.html: Ban Ton Tan market is Sunday only. Come on a weekday and you'll find a quiet temple with nothing trading. Check your dates before driving out — and arrive in the morning. By mid-afternoon several vendors start packing up, so earlier is better for the full spread.

When you're walking these markets, it helps to know what to actually order. Here are Saraburi's signature dishes and snacks, found across the old-town markets and city shops, ranked by how often people specifically come here for them.

items.name: Saraburi Curry Puffs (Kari Pap)
items.blurb: The province's number-one souvenir and it earns it. Flaky, layered pastry with fillings of chicken curry, potato, taro, and beans — both savoury and sweet versions available. The well-known Kari Pap Khun Joom has multiple branches in the city. Good to eat on the spot or take home.

items.name: Phat Mi Jae (Tai Yuan Stir-Fried Noodles)
items.blurb: A gently flavoured stir-fried rice noodle dish from the Tai Yuan Lanna community. Found mainly at the Ban Ton Tan water market — regular city restaurants rarely carry it. An ancient recipe tied to the Pa Sak riverside community.
items.meta: Ban Ton Tan market, Sundays only · THB 30–50/plate

items.name: Khao Man Gai — Old-School Recipe
items.blurb: Poached chicken rice the old way, as served at places like Jia Ko Pung. Silky chicken, soft rice, three-flavour dipping sauce, and a bowl of house-made pickled-lime soup on the side. Opens early — it's the right breakfast before driving up the hill.

items.name: Saraburi Boat Noodles
items.blurb: Rich, concentrated broth in the original tradition — thin or wide noodles, clear or 'nam tok' style. Pairs with pork satay and fried sides. Several well-known spots around the city centre. A lighter meal that still fills you up.

items.name: Khanom Kong + Old-Formula Fish Cakes
items.blurb: Khanom kong are wheel-shaped fried dough sweets, lightly fragrant. The old-recipe fish cakes alongside them are the kind of thing Ban Ton Tan still makes but most city markets don't. Buy a bag while you walk.
items.meta: Ban Ton Tan / old markets · THB 20–40/piece or bag

items.name: Dairy and Milk Sweets from the Dairy Farm Belt
items.blurb: Saraburi is known for its dairy farms around Muak Lek. Fresh milk, yoghurt, and milk-based sweets are easy to find at markets and shops around the city. A popular thing to bring back, especially for kids.

blocks.text: How to Fit the Old Town Into a Hills Trip

blocks.html: The appeal of Saraburi's old quarter is that it slots neatly into a Khao Yai or Muak Lek trip without eating the whole day. Here are two itineraries that work — pick based on which day you're coming.

blocks.label: Option 1
blocks.title: Sunday — Ban Ton Tan First, Then Head for the Hills

items.activity: Start at Ban Ton Tan Water Market, Sao Hai district
items.note: Come early for the full spread — try Phat Mi Jae, khanom kong, fish cakes, and a walk along the Pa Sak

items.activity: Leave the market, drive toward Muak Lek / Khao Yai
items.note: About 40–60 min to the waterfall and dairy farm zone

items.activity: Muak Lek waterfall or dairy farm visit
items.note: Swim, take photos, stop at a hillside café

items.activity: Pick up curry puffs on the way back through town
items.note: Take some home or eat them on the road

blocks.label: Option 2
blocks.title: Weekday — Hills First, Evening in the City

items.activity: Khao Man Gai breakfast at an old-school city shop
items.note: Eat before driving up — shops open early

items.activity: Head to the waterfall / Phra Phutthabat / dairy farms
items.note: Pick your lane: nature or temple

items.activity: Come back into town, walk Sukhumal Market
items.note: Look at the old shophouses, stop at Jae Siam's for a plate

items.activity: Dinner at the railway night market
items.note: Fried snacks, rice porridge, desserts to close out

blocks.title: A Car Makes This Much Easier
blocks.html: These spots are spread across different zones — the city centre, Sao Hai, and Muak Lek. Driving yourself or renting a car gives you the most flexibility. Sukhumal Market and the night market are central with street parking nearby. Ban Ton Tan has its own parking lot.

faq.q: When is the Ban Ton Tan Ancient Water Market open?
faq.a: Sundays only, 08:00–16:00, in Sao Hai district on the Pa Sak River. There's parking on site. Come on a weekday and you'll find nothing trading. Morning to mid-morning gives you the best selection before vendors start packing up.

faq.q: Where's the best place to eat in Saraburi's old quarter?
faq.a: Sukhumal Market (Talat Nai) in the city centre is the most active old-shophouse area — walk the alleyways for à la carte restaurants, old-school coffee shops, and street snacks. Right next to it is the railway night market, which is the go-to dinner spot for locals.

faq.q: What's the best souvenir to bring back from Saraburi?
faq.a: Curry puffs are the province's signature take-home food — multiple flavours, both savoury and sweet. Kari Pap Khun Joom is the well-known brand with several city branches. After that: dairy products from the Muak Lek farm belt, and khanom kong ancient sweets from Ban Ton Tan market.

faq.q: Should I visit the old town before or after going to the hills?
faq.a: On a Sunday, do the Ban Ton Tan market first (opens at 08:00) then drive up to Muak Lek. On a weekday, go to the hills first and come back to Sukhumal Market and the night market for dinner in the city.

faq.q: Is Saraburi easy to get to?
faq.a: Saraburi sits on the Mittraphap Highway, roughly 1.5–2 hours from Bangkok by car. The attractions are spread across different zones, so driving yourself or renting a car is the most practical option. Central markets have parking nearby.
